result:
Use the JSONL ledger.

The deciding factor is that humans read these records. JSONL is readable with `tail`, `grep`, and a text editor, diffs cleanly in git, and survives without any tooling. SQLite requires a client for every read, and a binary file in version control gives you no useful history.

The usual reasons to pick SQLite do not apply here. Concurrent writes are impossible in a single-threaded single-machine harness, so you gain no transactional safety you need. Scale is about 5,000 lines a year, which any script can read fully into memory, so indexes buy nothing. A schema would cost you migrations every time you add a field, while JSONL absorbs new keys with no ceremony.

Two things to accept with the append-only choice: corrections become new lines rather than edits, so readers need a "last record for this run id wins" rule; and ad hoc analysis needs `jq` or a short script instead of SQL.

Switch to SQLite if any of these becomes true: you need aggregate queries often enough that writing them in SQL beats scripting, you need to mutate past records in place, or a second writer appears. The migration is cheap in that direction, since you can load a JSONL file into SQLite with one command.
